tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve remaining disks after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After moving the current largest needed disk to its goal peg, treat the remaining smaller disks as a new subproblem and solve it recursively. This reduces the problem size step by step until all disks are correctly placed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest disk that still needs to be positioned has just been moved to its final peg and smaller disks remain unsolved.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a small disk onto the final peg before the larger disk that should be below it, creating an unsolvable ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target. This classic pattern respects the size rule at every step.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous stack of disks while preserving their order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move the bottom disk while smaller disks remain on top, violating the rule that only the topmost disk may be moved.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a single, syntactically correct list of moves in bracket notation; any preceding or trailing text may cause the parser to miss or mis‑interpret the list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very end of your answer, after all reasoning and checks are complete.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending explanatory sentences after the move list, which prevents the verifier from extracting the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure the final configuration matches the goal exactly. This catches missing or misplaced moves before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, after the move list has been written.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was not simulated.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should contain just the move list and nothing else (no explanations, duplicate lists, or comments). Any extra characters can break the parser.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the final output, after you have verified the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a header like "Final answer:" before the list, which adds non‑list characters to the output.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk. This guarantees every move obeys the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of each move, right before appending it to the list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg where disk 1 is on top, violating the larger‑onto‑smaller rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks to another peg so the larger disk can be placed safely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 5 onto peg 2 while disk 1 remains on peg 2, creating an illegal larger‑onto‑smaller placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, unless you plan to move the small disk away first. This prevents blocking the required ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk during the solution.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Temporarily moving disk 1 onto the final peg before disk 5 has been placed there, later blocking the placement of disk 5.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg (auxiliary or target) before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg, relocate those smaller disks to any other peg (including the target) before moving the larger disk. This frees the larger disk for a legal move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is not topmost because smaller disks sit above it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 2 remains on top of it, making the move impossible.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move a free larger disk to its target when possible
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a larger disk is the topmost disk on its current peg and its destination peg is empty or has only larger disks, move it directly to its target peg. This is the key step after the target peg has been cleared.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have cleared the target peg and ensured the larger disk is free.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving a free larger disk on its source peg even though its target peg is ready, resulting in unnecessary extra moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model finishes reasoning without outputting any moves, often due to early termination or forgetting to produce the final answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a move list as the final output, even if it is empty (but must be a valid list).

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model's generation stops before completing the full sequence, possibly due to token limits or premature stopping.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the move list is fully generated; if needed, plan the moves in advance and verify completeness before output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of which disk is currently on top after several moves, leading to illegal source moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an updated mental representation of each peg after every move and only select the topmost disk as the source.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a smaller disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks that need to be placed below it, blocking the required ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only move a small disk onto the final target peg after all larger disks that belong below it have been placed, or move it away before placing larger disks.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model checks only the source peg for topmost status and forgets to verify that the destination peg's top disk is larger, leading to a violation of the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, confirm that the destination peg is empty or its topmost disk is larger than the moving disk; if not, relocate the smaller disk first.
